messages:
priya: Heads up — several customers reporting console usage hours are ~6h behind since ~03:00 UTC. Dashboards show last_updated 02:50 for most tenants. Anyone started debugging? :thinking:

mike: saw alerts from hourly-rollup job around 03:10 — consumer lag spiked and a bunch of rollup tasks retried. Looking now.

ingest-oncall: posting logs from the rollup worker (cut to relevant lines):
```
2026-03-17T03:07:42Z ERROR hourly_rollup worker-12 tenant=acme failed to write partition hour=2026-03-17T02:00:00Z reason=WriterError(schema_mismatch)
2026-03-17T03:07:43Z WARN aggregator skipped 342 rows for tenant=acme hour=2026-03-17T02:00:00Z watermark=2026-03-17T02:59:59Z
2026-03-17T03:08:01Z INFO consumer group=analytics-ingest lag=12500 partitions_stalled=3
```

sam: can someone run a quick check on row counts for the hourly_rollups table vs raw_cdc for the affected hours? SQL to try: 
```sql
SELECT hour, count(*) FROM hourly_rollups WHERE tenant_id IN (123,345,678) AND hour BETWEEN '2026-03-17 02:00' AND '2026-03-17 06:00' GROUP BY hour ORDER BY hour;
```

priya: running that now, will paste results shortly. Affected tenants so far: 123(acme), 345(nimblepay), 678(voyager). Some are reporting incorrect billing charts too.

priya: results:
02:00 -> 0 rows (expected ~1800)
03:00 -> 1785 rows
04:00 -> 1799 rows
05:00 -> 1801 rows

elaine: 0 rows at 02:00 suggests ingestion wrote data into a mismatched partition key (tz or rounding bug). We had a recent change to the partitioner in ingest-worker v2.2.1. Could be off-by-one-hour mapping for DST/tz edge?

mike: digging through the ingest worker traces — I see some messages for hour=2026-03-17T01:00:00Z that have event_ts in the 02:xx range. That implies the aggregator watermark logic dropped rows because they appeared "too late" for the 02:00 window.

support-eng: do we have a repro query to surface raw events that were dropped? Maybe join raw_cdc by event_id to see where they landed.

mike: yes — this shows raw events with event_ts in 02:xx that were written to partition hour=01:00 by the new partitioner:
```sql
SELECT event_id, event_ts, written_hour, tenant_id FROM raw_cdc WHERE tenant_id=123 AND event_ts BETWEEN '2026-03-17 02:00' AND '2026-03-17 02:59' AND written_hour != date_trunc('hour', event_ts);
```
Found ~1.7k rows.

ingest-oncall: hypothesis: partitioner v2.2.1 used server-local timezone for date_trunc instead of normalizing to UTC, so some messages from UTC 02:xx were stamped written_hour=01:00 on workers in us-east zone. Aggregator watermark then considered them late and dropped them.

priya: that would explain why only a subset of tenants are affected (those routed to a worker on the different tz host). Good catch.

elaine: mitigation options: 1) reprocess the raw_cdc for the 02:00 hour for affected tenants into proper partitions (backfill), 2) patch partitioner to normalize to UTC and redeploy, 3) run a temporary aggregator fallback that accepts out-of-window rows for the next 6 hours. I prefer 1+2.

support-eng: agree. What are ETA and impact on query load?

mike: I can trigger a targeted reingest backfill for tenants 123,345,678 for hour=02:00. It will read raw_cdc events where written_hour=01:00 but event_ts between 02:00-02:59 and re-write into hour=02:00. Estimated time ~2-3 hours. I'll kick it off and post job id.

ingest-oncall: airflow trigger command I used:
```bash
airflow dags trigger reingest_hourly_backfill --conf '{"tenants":[123,345,678], "hours":["2026-03-17T02:00:00Z"]}'
```
Job id: backfill.2026-03-17.0023. Monitoring logs at https://airflow.internal/redwood/backfill. ETA 2.5h.

priya: thanks. I've informed the support cases and set customer-facing messages: "We're running a targeted backfill; dashboards should refresh in ~3 hours. Sorry for the disruption."

elaine: also filing a bug for the partitioner tz normalization — tag eng-runtime and eng-ml. Add postmortem, include quick regression test for date_trunc normalization.

support-eng: will update affected billing charts if needed after backfill completes. Marking this thread for incident follow-up. :white_check_mark:
